neighbours.label: the word piece that completes a compound name after 'South' (South|sea, South|port, South|ham|pton) or after 'Mid-' / 'half-' (Mid-S|outh, Mid| North, half-st|aff); a list, not a general rule: half-time, Mid-Atlantic and midsummer do not fire
fire: Flags at the courthouse were lowered to half-staff on Friday morning.
The wrestling show was held at the Mid-South arena near Memphis.
A hovercraft crosses from Southsea to the island in ten minutes.
Several surf towns along the Mid North Coast were cut off by floods.
The family took a summer holiday in Southport when the children were small.
The liner sailed from Southampton on a grey April afternoon.
The president ordered all flags flown at half-staff until sunset.
He grew up near the pier in Southsea and learned to sail there.
quiet: Flags at the courthouse were raised again on Friday morning.
The wrestling show was held at the big arena near Memphis.
A hovercraft crosses from the mainland to the island in ten minutes.
Several surf towns along the northern coast were cut off by floods.
The family took a summer holiday in Blackpool when the children were small.
The liner sailed from Liverpool on a grey April afternoon.
The president ordered all offices closed until sunset.
He grew up near the pier in Brighton and learned to sail there.

notes: Weak pole (max 4.47). Probes: half-staff, Mid-South, Southsea, Mid North 0.88-0.99, Southport 0.52, Southfield 0.15, half-time / Mid-Atlantic / midsummer 0.02-0.06. The − pole is 'half a dozen / half a century / semi-final'.
